back: All the methods used to inform customers, persuade them to buy and remind them of the product.
Advertising is a paid message in the media. Sales promotion is a short-term offer such as a discount, coupon or free sample.
Personal selling is face-to-face selling, suited to costly or technical goods. Direct marketing sends messages straight to chosen customers.
PR builds good relations. Publicity is unpaid media coverage the firm cannot control. Sponsorship pays to link the brand with an event or person.
Giving a product a name, symbol or design that makes it recognisable and different, to build loyalty.
Percentage of sales; objective and task; competitive parity; affordable. Each has a weakness: for example the percentage of sales method cuts spending when sales fall.
Depends on the product, market, budget, stage of the life cycle, objective and rivals' promotion.
Net gain = extra units × contribution per unit − cost of the campaign. Cost per extra unit sold = cost ÷ extra units.
Compare sales before, during and after, allowing for other causes such as season, price and rivals. Also count enquiries and coupons used.
